title: gather-migration-inputs.js off-by-one: half-open getStakersRange treated as inclusive drops the last staker of every pool, making the leg1 (and leg2) count preflight permanently unsatisfiable (suite DoS) with misleading 're-run gather' guidance
location: scripts/gather-migration-inputs.js:271-284 (end = Math.min(start+PAGE_SIZE, countNum) - 1 passed as exclusive end); contract semantics lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:662-678 (getStakersRange half-open [start,end))
description: StableStaker.getStakersRange(token, start, end) returns the half-open slice [start, end) — its NatSpec says so. The gather script computes end = min(start+200, count) - 1 and passes it as if inclusive, so every page silently loses its final element; with counts <= 200 this is exactly the last staker of each pool. Empirically on a quiescent fork: DOLA fetched 2 of stakerCount 3 (dropped 0x25AdA296…), USDC fetched 5 of 6 (dropped 0x0f254C40…). The script then (a) prints a WARNING attributing the mismatch to 'stakers joined between reads' and advising a re-run — which can never converge because the bug is deterministic — and (b) writes count = fetched length into leg1-stakers.json. SkimAndLeg1Migration's preflight requires that count to equal live stakerCount exactly, so leg1 (preview AND broadcast) reverts 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count … re-run gather' forever. The SAME pager is used for --leg 2, so the gather for Leg2Migration against the temp staker inherits the identical block (count=2 DOLA / count=5 USDC), halting leg2 fail-loud at its own count-equality preflight.
impact: Hard, deterministic denial of the entire story-060 migration runbook at step 2 (and again at step 4) until the JS is fixed or the input file is hand-built. Fail-safe today only by accident of double-bookkeeping: had the script written the on-chain count instead of the fetched length, the preflight would pass and the dropped staker would be silently stranded in a terminally-migrating pool (recoverable only via permissionless userMigrate or a manual migrator batch). Operator time is also burned by the actively wrong 're-run' guidance.

classification.assetImpact: None. The off-by-one drops the last staker per pool, making the count-equality preflight unsatisfiable, so leg1 (and leg2) revert fail-loud before any funds move.
attackPath: 1. gather-migration-inputs.js treats half-open getStakersRange [start,end) as inclusive, dropping the final staker of each page.
2. It writes count = fetched length (under by one) and prints misleading 're-run gather' guidance that never converges.
3. SkimAndLeg1Migration preflight requires count==live stakerCount; reverts permanently. Same pager bricks leg2 at its own gate.
classification.likelihood: Deterministic suite DoS at two gates, but fail-loud with no partial state and no fund movement (fail-safe by double-bookkeeping accident).
classification.assumptions: Fix is a JS one-liner (use half-open end directly); had the script written on-chain count instead, the dropped staker would have been silently stranded — but as written it fails loud.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond fixing the JS or hand-building the input file.

evidence: side-effects.json inputGathering (gathered 2/3 and 5/6 on a quiescent fork; dropped addresses identified) and executed[0] (exact leg1 preflight revert). Input fixup #1 (hand-rebuilt JSON from getStakers()) immediately unblocks the preflight. leg2 recurrence: leg2-entry side-effects.json gatherResult + unmodifiedPreview revert 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count in leg2-stakers.json - re-run gather', 2 != 3; leg2-stakers.BUGGY-LEG1-02.json captured.
recommendation: Use the half-open convention: const end = Math.min(start + PAGE_SIZE, countNum); pass end directly and advance start = end. Make the fetched-vs-count mismatch FATAL (process.exit(2)) rather than a non-fatal warning so the gatherer cannot emit an under-count file, and cross-check the final list against getStakers() when count <= a sanity bound. Applies identically to leg 1 and leg 2.
dedupNotes: COLLAPSED leg1 idx1 (LEG1-02, canonical root cause, Medium) and leg2 idx1 (same code path against the temp staker, raw severity Low, self-labeled 'duplicate root cause of LEG1-02, do not double-count'). One root cause OffByOnePagination; leg2 recurrence folded as impact-scope evidence. Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Severity stays Medium (driven by the leg1 hard-DoS). The leg2 instance's fail-loud halt is the same defect reaching a second gate, not a new finding.
sanitizationReason: New entry point migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Off-by-one half-open-range JS bug -> hard suite DoS. Not any KI; not an admin-trust/weird-token class. Distinct from all ledger entries. NEW.
severityJustification: Hard but fully fail-loud availability bug with no fund movement, no partial state, and a trivial JS one-line fix, so per the calibration (prefer Low for clean-revert availability bugs with trivial fixes) this is Low rather than Medium. It denies the runbook deterministically, which is real operational pain, but the double-bookkeeping makes it fail safe before any on-chain mutation and the misleading 're-run' guidance is a footgun aggravator, not an asset/value risk.
